# generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is **“perform the two-axis reflection only when the vertical color-5 guide is perfectly continuous; otherwise leave the grid unchanged.”** It fits all canonical demonstrations because their guide intersection belongs to the vertical guide (color 5), so the vertical guide never has a gap.

An exact disagreement input is stored in `repo/generators/aad4e3a1d5e3/counterexamples/require_unbroken_vertical_guide.json` (seed 0, sample index 1, medium). It is a 10x12 lawful scene whose horizontal color-6 guide owns the intersection, so the vertical 5-guide is broken at one cell. The intended rule mirrors the two-color motif into all four quadrants; the shortcut returns the input unchanged.

I checked the case three ways:

1. `workspace/probe_shortcut.py` verifies that the shortcut fits every usable canonical pair, the generated input passes `self_check`, and the rival disagrees with the independent Python rule mirror.
2. `checks/shortcut-witness-racket.json` executes the selected Racket authority (`3fcc1761aea7`) on that exact input.
3. The Racket output equals the Python intended output and differs from the rival output; those booleans and both outputs are retained in the counterexample JSON.

Yes. The proposed generator emits these cases by construction: every odd position of its eight-sample schedule is horizontal-owned. In any five consecutive samples, at least two such witnesses occur, so any one query holdout leaves a refuting demonstration. The 300-lesson census and the exhaustive fixed-seed schedule census found zero surviving declared rivals in production or any query rotation.
